## 

```{r}
# data on HITTERS ISLR2 and salary 

# prep, train , test split,  ols, regression diagnostics, fwd and bwd selection, ridge and lasso , pca, partial least square , test set model comparison , bootstrap internal validation 

library(ISLR2)
library(Hmisc)
library(rms)
#install.packages("leaps")
library(leaps)
library(glmnet)
library(pls)

# data d <- on Hitters from ISLR2

d <- ISLR2::Hitters
dim(d)
names(d)
sum(is.na(d$Salary))
d <- na.omit(d)
dim(d)
colSums(is.na(d))

```

#explore the data and lets do some data wrangling

```{r}
Hmisc::describe(d)
summary(d$Salary)

par(mfrow = c(2,2))
hist(d$Salary, 
     main = "Salary Distribution",
     xlab = "Salary ($1,000s)")

plot(d$Hits, d$Salary,
     main = "Hits vs Salary",
     xlab = "Hits", ylab = "Salary")

plot(d$Years, d$Salary,
     main =  "Expereince vs. Salary",
     xlab = "Years", ylab = "Salary")

boxplot(Salary ~ League, data = d,
        main = "Salary by League", 
        ylab = "Salary")

par(mfrow = c(1,1))


# correlation among continous variable 

Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(d[, c("Salary", "Hits", "AtBat", "Years", "CAtBat")])
             )


```

```{r}

set.seed(2026)

train_id <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(d)),
  size = floor(0.70 * nrow(d))
)

train <- d[train_id, ]
test <- d[-train_id, ]

nrow(train)
nrow(test)


lm_small <- lm(
  Salary ~ Hits + HmRun + Walks + Years, 
  data = train
)

summary(lm_small)


lm_full <- lm(Salary ~ ., data = train)

summary(lm_small)$r.squared
summary(lm_full)$r.squared

AIC(lm_small, lm_full)
BIC(lm_small, lm_full)
par(mfrow = c(2,3))
plot(lm_small, which = 1:6)
```

```{r}

# rms regression modeling and strategies and diagnostics 

dd_hitters <- rms::datadist(train)
options(datadist = "dd_hitters")

rms_fit <- rms::ols(
  Salary ~ Hits + HmRun + Walks + Years, 
  data = train, 
  x = TRUE,
  y = TRUE
)

print(rms_fit)
anova(rms_fit)
plot(rms::Predict(rms_fit, Hits))
plot(rms::Predict(rms_fit, Years))

# Examine the best models with up to 10 predictors
best_fit <- leaps::regsubsets(
Salary ~ .,
data = train,
nvmax = 10,
method = "exhaustive"
)


best_results <- summary(best_fit)

# Compare model sizes
best_results$rsq
best_results$adjr2
best_results$cp
best_results$bic

best_size <- which.min(best_results$bic)
best_size

best_coef <- coef(best_fit, id = best_size)
best_coef

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(best_results$rsq, type = "b",
xlab = "Number of predictors",
ylab = "R-squared")
plot(best_results$adjr2, type = "b",
xlab = "Number of predictors",
ylab = "Adjusted R-squared")
plot(best_results$cp, type = "b",
xlab = "Number of predictors",
ylab = "Mallows Cp")
plot(best_results$bic, type = "b",
xlab = "Number of predictors",
ylab = "BIC")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
# Which predictors were selected?
plot(best_fit, scale = "bic")
```

```{r}

# forward and backward selection 

forward_fit <- leaps::regsubsets(
  Salary ~ ., 
  data = train,
  nvmax = 10,
  method = "forward"
)

backward_fit <- leaps::regsubsets(
  Salary ~ .,
  data = train, 
  nvmax = 10,
  method = "backward"
)
forward_size <- which.min(summary(forward_fit)$bic)
backward_size <- which.min(summary(backward_fit)$bic)


# Examine the selected coefficients
coef(forward_fit, id = forward_size)
coef(backward_fit, id = backward_size)
# Compare the selected model sizes
c(Best = best_size,
Forward = forward_size,
Backward = backward_size)



# glmnet needs numeric matrices instead of a formula.
# model.matrix automatically encodes categorical predictors.
x_train <- model.matrix(
Salary ~ ., data = train
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
x_test <- model.matrix(
Salary ~ ., data = test
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
y_train <- train$Salary
y_test <- test$Salary
dim(x_train)
dim(x_test)
# Common CV fold assignments for ridge and lasso
set.seed(2026)
fold_id <- sample(
rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(train))
)






```

```{r}

cv_ridge <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
  x = x_train,
  y = y_train,
  family = "gaussian",
  alpha = 0,
  foldid = fold_id,
  type.measure = "mse",
  standardize = TRUE
)
plot(cv_ridge)

cv_ridge$lambda.min


cv_ridge$lambda.min
# More regularized one-SE choice
cv_ridge$lambda.1se
# Ridge coefficients
coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.min")
# Coefficient paths
plot(cv_ridge$glmnet.fit, xvar = "lambda")



```

```{r}

# alpha = 1 specifies LASSO
# LASSO can set coefficients exactly to zero.
cv_lasso <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
x = x_train,
y = y_train,
family = "gaussian",
alpha = 1,
foldid = fold_id,
type.measure = "mse",
standardize = TRUE
)
plot(cv_lasso)
cv_lasso$lambda.min
cv_lasso$lambda.1se
# Selected coefficients
coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.min")
# Count nonzero predictor coefficients
sum(
as.vector(coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.min"))[-1] != 0
)
# LASSO coefficient paths
plot(cv_lasso$glmnet.fit, xvar = "lambda")

```

```{r}
# 11. PRINCIPAL COMPONENTS REGRESSION --------------------
# Use the same numeric predictors as glmnet.
# Scale predictors within the model.
pcr_train <- data.frame(
Salary = y_train,
x_train,
check.names = FALSE
)
pcr_test <- data.frame(
x_test,
check.names = FALSE
)
set.seed(2026)
pcr_fit <- pls::pcr(
Salary ~ .,
data = pcr_train,
scale = TRUE,
ncomp = 10,
validation = "CV",
segments = 5
)
summary(pcr_fit)
# CV prediction error by number of components
validationplot(pcr_fit, val.type = "MSEP")
# Choose a parsimonious number of components
pcr_ncomp <- pls::selectNcomp(
pcr_fit,
method = "onesigma",
plot = FALSE
)
pcr_ncomp
```

```{r}


# 12. PARTIAL LEAST SQUARES -------------------------------
set.seed(2026)
pls_fit <- pls::plsr(
Salary ~ .,
data = pcr_train,
scale = TRUE,
ncomp = 10,
validation = "CV",
segments = 5
)
summary(pls_fit)
validationplot(pls_fit, val.type = "MSEP")
pls_ncomp <- pls::selectNcomp(
pls_fit,
method = "onesigma",
plot = FALSE
)
pls_ncomp
```

```{r}

# 13. FINAL TEST-SET COMPARISON --------------------------
# All tuning above used training data only.
# Now evaluate the models on test, once.
# OLS predictions
pred_small <- predict(lm_small, newdata = test)
pred_full <- predict(lm_full, newdata = test)
# Best-subset predictions
# Extract exactly the columns in the selected model.
subset_test_matrix <- model.matrix(
Salary ~ ., data = test
)
pred_subset <- as.numeric(
subset_test_matrix[, names(best_coef), drop = FALSE] %*%
best_coef
)
# Ridge predictions
pred_ridge <- as.numeric(
predict(cv_ridge,
newx = x_test,
s = "lambda.min")
)
# LASSO predictions
pred_lasso <- as.numeric(
predict(cv_lasso,
newx = x_test,
s = "lambda.min")
)
# PCR and PLS predictions
pred_pcr <- as.numeric(
predict(pcr_fit,
newdata = pcr_test,
ncomp = pcr_ncomp)
)
pred_pls <- as.numeric(
predict(pls_fit,
newdata = pcr_test,
ncomp = pls_ncomp)
)
# Compare test MSE

results <- data.frame(
Model = c("OLS small", "OLS full", "Best subset",
"Ridge", "LASSO", "PCR", "PLS"),
MSE = c(
mean((y_test - pred_small)^2),
mean((y_test - pred_full)^2),
mean((y_test - pred_subset)^2),
mean((y_test - pred_ridge)^2),
mean((y_test - pred_lasso)^2),
mean((y_test - pred_pcr)^2),
mean((y_test - pred_pls)^2)
)
)
# Convert to RMSE (same salary units as the outcome)
results$RMSE <- sqrt(results$MSE)
# Rank by test RMSE
results <- results[order(results$RMSE), ]
print(results)
# Visual comparison
barplot(
results$RMSE,
names.arg = results$Model,
las = 2,
ylab = "Test RMSE (salary in $1,000s)",
main = "Model Comparison"
)


# This validates the specified rms OLS model.
# It does NOT validate the entire model-selection pipeline.
set.seed(2026)
validation <- rms::validate(
rms_fit,
method = "boot",
B = 200
)
print(validation)
# Look at optimism-corrected R2 and MSE,
# plus the optimism-corrected calibration slope.

```
